title: Mermaid Software Diagrams Questionnaire
concept: Choosing and authoring software-oriented Mermaid diagrams

questions.prompt: Which diagram best explains who sends each message during an order request and in what order?
questions.explanation: Correct: a sequence diagram places messages along a top-to-bottom time axis. Incorrect options: a class diagram describes static types and relationships; an ER diagram describes data entities and cardinality, not runtime order.

questions.prompt: Which sequence-diagram block expresses two mutually exclusive outcomes such as approved and rejected?
questions.explanation: Correct: `alt` and `else` model alternative branches. Incorrect options: `loop` communicates repetition; `par` communicates concurrent branches rather than exclusive outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which class relationship says an Order strongly owns its OrderLine parts?
questions.explanation: Correct: `*--` is composition, a strong whole-part relationship. Incorrect options: `..>` is a dependency without ownership; `<|--` means inheritance and would claim an OrderLine is a kind of Order.

questions.prompt: Which relationship most clearly shows StripeGateway realizing the PaymentGateway interface?
questions.explanation: Correct: `<|..` is Mermaid's UML-style realization relationship. Incorrect options: composition means strong ownership; a plain solid link does not communicate interface implementation.

questions.prompt: In a state diagram, which line declares Draft as the initial state?
questions.explanation: Correct: an arrow from `[*]` enters the initial state. Incorrect options: an arrow into `[*]` marks a terminal transition; `actor` is sequence-diagram syntax and does not declare state-machine entry.

options.label: PendingPayment contains an internal state machine.
PendingPayment is a database entity with attributes.

questions.explanation: Correct: the braced state body defines a composite state with nested states. Incorrect options: database attributes belong to ER syntax; parallel messages belong to a sequence `par` block.

questions.prompt: How should `CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places` be read?

options.label: Each order has exactly one customer; a customer may have zero or many orders.
Each order has many customers; a customer must have exactly one order.
Customer sends an asynchronous runtime message to Order.

questions.explanation: Correct: `||` is exactly one and `o{` is zero or more. Incorrect options: the reversed cardinalities contradict the markers; ER relationships describe data associations, not runtime messages.

questions.prompt: The team needs to decide whether a cancelled order may later become confirmed. Which diagram is the best primary tool?

options.label: Sequence diagram of one successful request

questions.explanation: Correct: a state diagram exposes legal and forbidden lifecycle transitions. Incorrect options: one successful sequence does not enumerate lifecycle rules; method structure does not prove which state changes are allowed.
